$comment: THE ONLY PERSON ON THE WIND STEP WHO IS NOT THERE FOR THE FIGHT. He is a steward at the mouth of the stewards' stair, and he is the whole staff of the middle of this building: he lights the fires above, he carries people down, and he thinks none of it is remarkable. He is what makes the Summit's standing order -- framed in the Last Room, cut into every lintel above -- read as an institution rather than as a mechanic. Nobody in the Summit is solemn. That is the Summit.

lines: Still here. Somebody has to be, and the fire will not keep itself in.
Whichever way it goes up there, you come down this stair and not through that slab.
Stewards' stair, and that door behind me is never locked. Nobody has ever locked it.
Four hundred and eleven steps down to the hall, and it comes out behind the rail.
